D.t: Hannah Pingree leads by 11.6 in the forecast and wins 97% of simulations. The cushion is about 86,157 votes; a one point swing is about 3,704 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +4.0 and D +19.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +11.3. Your best recent poll is Maine People's Resource Center (D) at D +14.3; your worst is University of New Hampshire at D +8.3. 10 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Cumberland, a projected net 72,734 votes; York, a projected net 20,736 votes; Hancock, a projected net 6,181 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Penobscot, R +8.5, 10.4% of the vote; Kennebec, R +0.2, 8.9% of the vote; Androscoggin, R +5.3, 7.1% of the vote; Oxford, R +8.6, 4.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Hannah Pingree runs furthest behind in Androscoggin, Penobscot, Kennebec. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 94% of voters, 51 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.68 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 76% of voters, 54 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.79 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 57 to 34, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.09 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Hannah Pingree: Immigration voters 26 to 64, Men 47 to 47, Midsize counties 47 to 47. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.2M cash against $395K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 50% of the 179,532 ballots in Maine so far, against 21% for the other party. That is 2.2 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points toward Hannah Pingree. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Money: Raised $509K against $1.2M for Hannah Pingree.

R.t: Bobby Charles trails by 11.6 and wins 3% of simulations. Closing it takes about 43,079 voters switching sides, or 86,157 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +19.0 and D +4.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +11.3. Your best recent poll is University of New Hampshire at D +8.3; your worst is Maine People's Resource Center (D) at D +14.3. 10 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Penobscot, a projected net 6,537 votes; Aroostook, a projected net 6,387 votes; Somerset, a projected net 5,421 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Penobscot, R +8.5, 10.4% of the vote; Kennebec, R +0.2, 8.9% of the vote; Androscoggin, R +5.3, 7.1% of the vote; Oxford, R +8.6, 4.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Bobby Charles runs furthest behind in Sagadahoc, York, Hancock. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 94% of voters, 43 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.68 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 76% of voters, 37 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.79 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 34 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.09 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Bobby Charles: Health care and Social Security voters 18 to 72, Large counties 27 to 68, Corruption voters 28 to 63. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$395K cash against $1.2M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Republicans cast 21% of the 179,532 ballots in Maine so far, against 50% for the other party. That is 2.2 points worse for Republicans than the forecast expected by now.

R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points away from Bobby Charles. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
